findings.title: stream_close() waiting on old _outgoing_queue_ready could miss in-flight frames
findings.claim: stream_close() now waits on the old _outgoing_queue_ready; the report checked whether frames accepted by send() before _stream_closing was set are properly written before the buffer closes, and whether concurrent stop_send_loop() is properly serialized via _sink_closed_future, and found no issue.

findings.title: Possible hang if stream_close() runs before negotiation finishes
findings.claim: The report considered whether the drain wait could hang if stream_close() ran before negotiation completed, checking both server (stream only registered after negotiation) and client (sink::close() only calls close_sink() after eof send resolves, which itself waits on negotiation) paths, and found no way for this to happen.

findings.title: Back-pressure from a non-reading peer can stall the drain
findings.claim: A peer that stops reading can stall the drain wait, but the report notes this is the same behavior as before since the old write_buf.close() blocked the same way, so it is not a new issue.

findings.title: New flag could be set multiple times or on non-stream connections
findings.claim: The report checked the new flag and confirmed it is only set on stream connections and only once, due to the !error() guard, so this is not a problem.

findings.title: New test asserts client_factory.hooks.size() == 2 assuming stream negotiation ordering
findings.claim: The new test asserts client_factory.hooks.size() == 2 before any data has gone over the stream, which assumes the client-side stream connection has already negotiated when call(...) returns; the report could not confirm this ordering is guaranteed and flagged the check could be flaky, but was not confident enough to call it a bug.
